description: This false-colour satellite image displays distinct land cover types, likely used for classification guidance within the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS). The image presents a landscape with varying tones of teal, brown, and bright red, indicative of different vegetation conditions. A yellow label box, "5.1.0 I Heathlands and Moorlands", points via a thin line to an area in the upper right quadrant of the image, which is primarily dark teal and crisscrossed by lighter lines, possibly paths. This area is further indicated by a yellow circular marker with a black outline. A second yellow label box, "Grassland", points to an area in the lower right quadrant, which appears in lighter brown/pinkish tones, also marked by a yellow circular point with a black outline. Distinct patches of bright red vegetation, possibly indicating vigorous plant growth or a specific vegetation type like heathland invading grasslands, are visible in the central-left and lower-left areas, but are not directly labelled by the pointers. The image is an example for visual interpretation in land use / land cover (LULC) mapping.
